body: Whether you show it or not, your feelings run deep, but you learned early to keep them behind glass. Closeness and self-protection pull against each other in you: you want to be held and you brace against needing it. This can make warmth feel rationed, or make steadiness feel like the only safe role. As an adult you can read as cool or self-sufficient when underneath you're starving for the reassurance you won't ask for. Toughening up was never the answer; the work is letting one safe person past the glass.
gift: At your best: loyal, dependable, emotionally honest once you trust.
shadow: The trap: deciding it's safer to need nothing, and calling that strength.
integration: Let care become part of your structure. Consistency matters, but it should include rest, softness, and people who do not require you to perform being fine.
do: Let one person in past the guard
Say the need out loud before it curdles into resentment
Treat warmth as something you build, not earn
dont: Test people instead of trusting them
